item.title: Two U.S. warplanes shot down; search ongoing in Iran for 1 missing crew member
item.summary: An F-15 fighter jet and an A-10 attack plane were lost to hostile fire. Two search-and-rescue helicopters also were hit, injuring the crews, before safely returning to their base, officials said.

item.title: Trump requests record-breaking budget of $1.5 trillion for Pentagon
item.summary: The budget proposes a 44 percent increase in defense spending, and Trump’s request comes as Congress grapples with the ballooning costs of the war in Iran.

item.title: Reeling from war in the Middle East, Trump reaches for a reset
item.summary: The president is in a precarious political moment seven months before the midterm elections, facing some of his lowest approval ratings and presiding over an unpopular war.

item.title: Hegseth forces out Army’s top general, two other senior officers
item.summary: Gen. Randy George’s ouster is the latest clash between the Pentagon chief and the service’s senior leadership, and comes during the war in Iran.

item.title: Trump proposes $10B fund for D.C. construction, beautification projects
item.summary: The planned Presidential Capital Stewardship Program would help renovate parks and infrastructure, as Trump works to remake a city he has derided as “dirty.”

item.title: Alleged D.C. pipe bomber might adopt debunked conspiracy theory as defense
item.summary: Brian Cole Jr. gave a detailed confession in December, but his defense attorneys suggested he could point at a Capitol Police officer who has been cleared in the case.

item.title: How Trump came to re-endorse a Republican congressman he had just ditched
item.summary: House leaders and lobbyists rallied around Rep. Jeff Hurd (Colorado) after Trump, angry about Hurd’s vote against tariffs, withdrew support for his reelection.

item.title: Panel led by Trump allies approves White House ballroom amid legal battle
item.summary: The vote by the National Capital Planning Commission on Thursday marked the final procedural hurdle for President Donald Trump’s plans.

item.title: Democrats, voter rights groups file lawsuits on Trump order on mail ballots
item.summary: The plaintiffs in both cases argue the president’s order violates the Constitution, which directly gives states and Congress the power to regulate federal elections and voter rolls.

item.title: Tracking who Trump is appointing to fill key administration roles
item.summary: Follow President Trump’s progress filling over 800 positions, among about 1,300 that require Senate confirmation, in this tracker from The Washington Post and the Partnership for Public Service.
